result.topic_en: Ramanujan gives formula (18), a closed form for a series involving 1/(e^{(2n-1)π}+1) and 1/((2n-1)^4+4α^4), and deduces that certain related infinite series can be expressed in finite terms when 2α or α is a positive integer, with a hyperbolic-sine example.
result.transcription:
and
(18) $\frac{1}{e^{\pi}+1}\cdot\frac{1}{1^4+4\alpha^4}+\frac{3}{e^{3\pi}+1}\cdot\frac{1}{3^4+4\alpha^4}+\frac{5}{e^{5\pi}+1}\cdot\frac{1}{5^4+4\alpha^4}+\dots$
$=\frac{\pi}{32\alpha^2}\cdot\left\{\frac{e^{\pi\alpha}-(-1)^\alpha}{e^{\pi\alpha}+(-1)^\alpha}\right\}^2$
$-\frac{1}{8\alpha}\left\{\frac{1}{(1-\alpha)^2+\alpha^2}+\frac{1}{(3-\alpha)^2+\alpha^2}+\dots\right.$ to $\alpha$ terms$\}$
It follows from (16) that, if $2\alpha$ be [-a-] positive integer, then
[-$\left\{\frac{1}{e^{2\pi}-1}-\frac{1}{e^{2\pi(1+2\alpha)}-1}\right\}$-] $\sum_{n=1}^{n=\infty}\left\{\frac{1}{e^{2n\pi}-1}-\frac{1}{e^{2\pi(n+2\alpha)}-1}\right\}\frac{1}{(n+\alpha)^2+\alpha^2}$
can be expressed in finite terms. Similarly from (18) we see that, if $\alpha$ be [-a-] positive integer, then
$\sum_{n=1}^{n=\infty}\left\{\frac{1}{e^{(2n-1)\pi}+1}-\frac{1}{e^{(2\alpha+2n-1)\pi}+1}\right\}\frac{1}{(2n-1+\alpha)^2+\alpha^2}$
can be expressed in finite terms.. For example
$\frac{1}{(1^2+2^2)(\sinh 3\pi-\sinh\pi)}+\frac{1}{(2^2+3^2)(\sinh 5\pi-\sinh\pi)}+\frac{1}{(3^2+4^2)(\sinh 7\pi-\sinh\pi)}+\dots$
$=\left(\frac{1}{\pi}+\coth\pi-\frac{1}{2}\pi\tanh^2\frac{1}{2}\pi\right)\Big/2\sinh\pi.$
